data.description:
## What happened

LLM-backed rebar operations hung **indefinitely** — 0.0% CPU, state `S` (sleeping), no output —
for **3 to 5 hours**, until killed. `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` defaults to 600 s and is wired into both
the Bedrock client (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:95` → `read_timeout`/`connect_timeout`) and a
wall-clock guard (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:376`), so **the configured timeout did not
fire**. This is not "no timeout exists" — it is "the timeout was bypassed or the hang is outside
the region it guards".

## Evidence (observed 2026-08-19/20)

Affected THREE independent sessions in three different worktrees simultaneously, so it is not
workspace-local:

| pid | op | worktree | elapsed | %CPU | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80532 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 80534 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 33196 | `review-plan` | noncodebase-tag | 3h20m | 0.0 | S |
| 31254 | `transition … closed` | impl-obese-dihedral-ermine | 3h41m | 0.0 | S |
| 33211 | `review-plan` | rp05-cli-registry | 3h37m | 0.0 | S |

Discriminating observations:

1. **Only LLM-invoking operations hang.** Every wedged process was `review-plan` or a
   `transition → closed` (which runs the completion verifier). In the same period, non-LLM store
   writes — `rebar session-log append`, `rebar edit`, `rebar comment`, `rebar set-file-impact`,
   `rebar link` — all completed in seconds.
2. **It is NOT store-lock contention.** `lsof .tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` showed **no
   holder** while seven processes were wedged. No per-ticket `.write.lock` existed for the
   affected tickets.
3. **It is NOT slow progress.** 0.0% CPU sustained over hours; a fresh probe run produced
   **zero bytes of output and zero CPU** rather than progressing slowly.
4. **At least one process did LLM work first, then blocked.** pid 33196 (`review-plan`) was
   observed at **87.7% CPU** at t+1h18m and at **0.0% CPU** at t+3h03m — so it completed
   compute and then wedged, which suggests the hang may be AFTER the model call (persisting the
   attestation / a git or network step) rather than in the call itself. This is the main
   ambiguity a root-cause pass must resolve.
5. Killing the wedged processes left every affected ticket cleanly in its prior status with no
   partial event written — the store was not corrupted.

## Why it matters

Every gated operation is affected: no work ticket can be claimed (plan-review gate) or closed
(completion-verification gate) while this is happening. It stalled an entire epic's board
bookkeeping for hours across multiple agent sessions, and the only escape hatch is
`--force=<reason>`, which records **no signed attestation** — i.e. the outage silently degrades
the audit trail if operators work around it.

## Suggested first step

Do NOT assume the model endpoint. The 87.7%→0.0% transition on pid 33196 makes a post-call hang
(attestation write, `git` subprocess, or a second uninstrumented network call) at least as
plausible as a hung provider socket. `/rebar-debug` with a hypothesis-driven pass is the right
protocol; a stack dump (`py-spy dump --pid <pid>`) of a live wedged process would settle it in
one observation, so capture one before killing the next occurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exact blocking call is identified by direct observation (stack dump of a wedged
      process), not inferred.
- [ ] An LLM-backed operation cannot exceed its configured `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` wall clock,
      whatever the blocking layer, and fails with a clear error naming the timed-out stage.
- [ ] A regression test drives the identified blocking layer to hang and asserts the operation
      aborts within the configured budget instead of sleeping indefinitely.
data.title: LLM-backed rebar ops hang for hours; REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT does not fire
